source_review.notes: Checked all six cited sources at OWASP, NIST, Google Research/USENIX, the RFC Editor, or PostgreSQL. OWASP API1:2023 confirms BOLA across client-supplied identifiers and per-object action checks; the Authorization Cheat Sheet confirms deny-by-default and per-request enforcement. NIST SP 800-162 supplies subject/object/action/environment ABAC semantics. The Zanzibar paper supports the explicitly bounded causal-consistency discussion. RFC 9110 confirms optional 404 concealment for forbidden resources. PostgreSQL 17 documents default-deny RLS when enabled without an applicable policy, USING/WITH CHECK behavior, and owner/superuser/BYPASSRLS exceptions.

evidence: Reviewed sets S, K, T, A, O, E; trusted context c=(s,k,t,g,q); object state and relationship functions; total decision D; authorized set O_{c,a}; and policy component predicates for consistent definitions.
Confirmed every TeX command is inside GitHub-compatible math delimiters and the allow predicate uses distinct validation, capability, relationship, attribute/state, and environment terms.
Confirmed PEP, PDP, authorized set, selector, horizontal/vertical/cross-tenant/contextual escalation, and TOCTOU terminology is defined before formal use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates a client selector from the policy-derived object set and distinguishes decision truth from enforcement coverage.

numerical_recomputation.notes: No probability, entropy threshold, benchmark, availability, latency, or quantitative risk claim is made. The timing numbers in Example 10 are a hypothetical side-channel trace, not empirical measurements.

evidence: Expanded allow(c,a,o,s) into context validity AND coarse capability AND relationship AND attribute/state AND environment checks, confirming each is necessary and an identifier is never sufficient.
Re-derived O_{c,a} as exactly the objects satisfying D(c,a,o)=allow and list output as F intersection O_{c,a}; neither construction can add an unauthorized object under the stated assumptions.

Re-derived the conditional-write argument: matching the authorized predicate and expected version in the authoritative operation prevents that operation from updating a different stored version under its assumed transaction semantics.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter explicitly bounds the set-safety result by policy correctness, trusted/current inputs, complete PEP coverage, and effect binding.

evidence: Reviewed absent, guessed, leaked UUID, global ID, cursor, nested relation, body/header ID, same-tenant peer, cross-tenant, public/private, archived/deleted/held, stale-version, ownership-transfer, and unknown-policy inputs.

Reviewed list/count/search/aggregate, GraphQL fields and node lookup, batches, creates, updates, cascades, exports/downloads, signed URLs, caches, async jobs, events, support/admin, direct database, and privileged RLS paths.

Reviewed TOCTOU, stale relationship/policy caches, policy outage, response/status/timing/cache existence oracles, ID walking, mixed-authority batches, revoked delegation, and service-account authority laundering.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The analysis covers horizontal, vertical, cross-tenant, contextual, alternate-path, temporal, and side-channel authorization failures.

evidence: Executed object-authorization-policy: owned and shared reads allowed, a cross-tenant read concealed, shared cancellation denied by relationship, owned open cancellation allowed, and shipped cancellation denied by state.
Confirmed the derived visible set contains three same-tenant owned/shared orders, including the shipped order because state restricts cancellation rather than read.

Checked deny-by-default, trusted tenant, every-member batch authorization, old-and-new mutation policy, version-bound effect, cache/artifact boundary, and no-implicit-admin-bypass invariants across exposition and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model validates representative policy branches; it does not establish cryptographic context validation, database isolation, distributed consistency, or route coverage.

proof_review.notes: No formal authorization-system, information-flow, noninterference, cryptographic capability, database-isolation, or distributed-consistency proof is claimed.

evidence: Confirmed the authorized-set safety statement names its assumptions and explicitly excludes policy intent, fact trust/freshness, bypass paths, and mutation races.
Confirmed the conditional-write argument is bounded by authoritative evaluation and transaction isolation, while external facts/effects require separate binding.
Confirmed UUID, gateway, central PDP, database RLS, causal consistency, tests, and executable code are never presented as universal proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Guarantees, mechanisms, design recommendations, examples, and verification obligations are labeled distinctly.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-046/report.json records one passing deterministic local policy execution with seven exact outcomes.

Production identity, PDP, relationship store, database, transaction, RLS, route/resolver coverage, concurrency, cache, object storage, job, side-channel, and penetration tests are presented as required future evidence, not completed measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live service, policy engine, database, authorization graph, cache, storage system, or attack exercise was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed selector versus authority, trusted context construction, hybrid role/attribute/relationship policy, authorized retrieval, list/graph/batch enforcement, create/update/transfer/delete state policy, effect binding, layered PEPs, RLS limits, cache/artifact/job authority, concealment/audit, and policy-versus-coverage testing as one coherent complete-mediation model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through context-requiring repository methods, canonical action registries, typed total policy input, conditional versioned writes, per-member batch contracts, actor-preserving jobs, bounded cache and signed-URL authority, non-bypass runtime database roles, safe decision logs, route-to-PEP coverage, cross-user/cross-tenant fixtures, shadow/canary policy rollout, and fail-closed outage behavior. Product policy and consistency bounds remain explicit governed choices.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins with the identifier misconception, derives trusted decision context and authorized sets, then extends the model across reads, mutations, concurrency, layers, caches, jobs, errors, and verification. Ten examples cover distinct selector, tenant, field, batch, race, graph, async, cache, RLS, and side-channel cases; five exercises progress from policy retrieval through unfamiliar scientific-instrument transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
